paper: Cristea, Dinu, Georgescu, Mihai, Uban - Automatic Discrimination between Inherited and Borrowed Latin Words in Romance Languages
languages: ro it fr es pt ca
data_and_license: Wiktionary templates + DEX (Romanian); licence not checked
method: Feature-based ML; orthographic and phonetic versions; word-etymon n-grams and alignment features
evaluation: Accuracy and weighted F1; F1 84.5-92.1 ort / 81.3-92.2 phon; avg ~90%
what_it_establishes: Direct word-etymon classifiers reach ~90% F1 on Romance; borrowed words closer to etymon (norm. dist ~0.28-0.31 vs ~0.38-0.56)
what_it_does_not_establish: Indo-Aryan; intermediate stage; calibration; contamination; semi-learned items remain an error source
residual_opportunity: Latent-intermediate pathway likelihood; calibrated probabilities; replication on their data as the Romance arm

paper: Kanojia, Kulkarni, Bhattacharyya, Haffari - Cognate Identification to improve Phylogenetic trees for Indian Languages
evidence_level: thesis s4.1 only (states it reproduces the CoDS-COMAD work); ACM version paywalled; correspondence not verified
method: XDice, string similarity, SVM/HMM alignment; lexicographer validation
evaluation: TP/FP counts (e.g., hi-sa 378 TP / 211 FP of 589)
what_it_establishes: (per thesis) Orthographic similarity finds tatsama cognates easily but misses tadbhavas
what_it_does_not_establish: Any tatsama/tadbhava classifier or attribution evaluation; historical definitions (uses descriptive ones); MIA stage
residual_opportunity: Distinction discussed but not computationally classified in inspected sources; classification contribution requires defined, validated labels
